text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000120 bills 99215 well above peers in every complexity band, including low-complexity visits, and its supportive documentation is too thin and partly questionable to offset that.","leaning":"pattern_consistent_with_upcoding","interpretation":"A sicker panel does not explain the excess: the by-complexity table shows this provider's 99215 share at roughly two to three times the all-provider share in every band, including patients with 0 or 1 conditions. Sampled low-complexity 99215s include upper respiratory infections (C0059945, C0061024) and follow-up encounters (C0060059, C0061022), visits that rarely warrant the highest level. The records review found no unsupported 99215s, which points the other way, but only 6 documented 99215s came back (about 1% of claims documented), so this is too thin to clear the provider. Note checks also raise doubts about whether the notes reflect the visits: 7 notes claim moderate-or-higher data review with no lab or test on the claim, and problem-list flags appear on low-complexity 99215 C0060385; C0059529 is both a supported 99215 and a data-flag example. A reviewer should first request a larger, targeted chart sample of low-complexity 99215s and the audit trail, and check whether the high-MDM notes such as C0059529 and C0061267 show templated or cloned content."}
